units.title: Canonical llr equals the explicit normalized tilt ratio a.e.
units.statement: For a σ-finite base μ and two integrable exponential tilts, Mathlib's canonical log-likelihood ratio of the f-tilt against the g-tilt agrees almost everywhere under the left tilted law with f−log Z_f−g+log Z_g.
assumptions: The common base μ is σ-finite.
f is measurable and both exp f and exp g are μ-integrable.
The equality is under the left tilt μ_f, which is the law used by relative Fisher information.

steps.title: Expand the left tilt
steps.text: Mathlib's left-tilt identity contributes f−log Z_f and leaves a base-to-right-tilt llr.

steps.title: Expand the right tilt
steps.text: The right-tilt identity contributes −g+log Z_g, while the self log ratio is zero.

steps.title: Transfer the null set
steps.text: The equality is first assembled μ-a.e. and then transported to μ_f because every tilted measure is absolutely continuous with respect to its base.

units.lean_statement: The right-hand side is written explicitly in the public theorem, so no hidden selected representative occurs in its interface.
units.lean_proof: The proof combines the three canonical Mathlib llr identities pointwise on a full-measure set and uses absolute continuity to change the a.e. measure.

sources.label: Lee–Shen–Tian, Lemma 2 proof, equation (11)
sources.scope: ASTIS exposes the normalized-density representative and its canonical RN relation, implicit in the paper calculation.

boundary: Almost-everywhere equality of values does not identify classical gradients of arbitrary representatives.
No Fisher-information, log-Sobolev, Talagrand or Wasserstein conclusion is included.

tests.scope: Explicit quadratic-fiber instance pins the left-law a.e. direction and all normalizer signs.

review.scope: A.e. measure direction, signs, integrability assumptions and canonical-versus-smooth boundary accepted.

units.title: The restricted-Gaussian relative score is constant
units.statement: For η≠0, the explicit normalized log-ratio representative of the quadratic fiber centered at y against the one centered at y′ has the constant gradient η⁻¹(y−y′). The paper consumer specializes to η>0.
assumptions: E is a complete real inner-product space.
η is nonzero; SPHMC and the cited restricted-Gaussian theorem use η>0.
The differentiated function is displayed explicitly and is not Mathlib's arbitrary canonical measurable llr representative.

steps.title: Differentiate the two quadratics
steps.text: The genuine Fréchet gradients are −η⁻¹(x−y) and −η⁻¹(x−y′).

steps.title: Discard only spatial constants
steps.text: The two log normalizers may depend on μ, η and the centers, but not on x, so their derivatives vanish.

steps.title: Cancel x
steps.text: Subtracting the two quadratic scores cancels x and leaves the center displacement with the source sign.

units.lean_statement: The base measure is arbitrary because only the x-independence of its two normalizers is used. No normalization or integrability premise is smuggled into this calculus theorem.
units.lean_proof: A private helper derives the genuine gradient of each quadratic from the norm-square derivative and the Hilbert duality map. The public proof removes constant normalizers and performs the linear cancellation.

sources.label: Lee–Shen–Tian equation (11)
sources.scope: Exact sign and η⁻¹ coefficient; this equation is cited in the route used by SPHMC Lemma 4.17.

boundary: The theorem does not differentiate the canonical measurable llr.
A representative-to-canonical-Fisher adapter, the strong-convex Gibbs LSI/T₂ backend and the W₂ contraction all remain separate red nodes.
